pr_body:
Similarly, how GET _nodes/usage API has a section for aggregations,
this adds a similar section for query types.

Interface details:
- Unlike aggregations section, queries section is without a break up on
  field types.
- Query types are deduplicated per search request  (e.g. if a search request
  has 1 bool query and 5 term queries, this is counted as 1 bool query and
  1 term query).

Implementation details:
- A new SearchUsageService is started on a node start. It tracks the
  usage of registered query types.
- Usage of queries is tracked on the successfull completion of
  Query phase. Queries are already rewritten by this stage, thus
  the reported query types could be different from query types
  submitted by a user (e.g. match query could be reported as term query)
- Reported stats besides user submitted queries include internally
  submitted queries (e.g. queries used by Security)
- knn search is reported as "knn_score_doc" query, that is how it is
  represented internally.

Closes #88908, #88821
pr_title: Add queries section into the _nodes/usage API
pr_comment: Hi @mayya-sharipova, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

@javanna Thanks for looking and raising important questions.

> don't we end up doing the counting at the shard level, hence each query counter will be multiplied by the number of shards that the index it targets is composed of? 

Yes, indeed, similar to the stats for aggregations, the counting is per shard request.  If there are two shards in a node that participated in a particular search request, we will multiple submitted requests by  2. 

> How do we expect this data to be consumed: per node or per cluster? What is the processing that we expect to happen on the consumer side of these added stats? Would it make sense to do the counting on the coordinating node instead, assuming that we want to count each query as one? Would we want to track how many indices each query targets?

For the context, for telemetry, we collect data from 3 sources: `_cluster/stats`, `_nodes/usage` and `_xpack/usage`. I wanted this to be similar how we report aggregations by adding a section for used query types in the [_nodes\usage](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/cluster-nodes-usage.html) API.  Nodes usage API reports stats per node (what features are used in a particular node), so I think it would be weird to report stats just for a coordinating node, don't you agree?    

Another thing I am not sure about if we can do a deep inspection of a search request  on a coordinating node to report what query types were used in it.

Alternatively, may be this type of stats should be better reside in `_cluster/stats`?

> What is the processing that we expect to happen on the consumer side of these added stats? 

This would be a better question for @giladgal .

> Nodes usage API reports stats per node (what features are used in a particular node), so I think it would be weird to report stats just for a coordinating node, don't you agree?

that's a good question. Maybe... but I think counts are off if they get multiplied by the number of shards, and we are probably looking at the wrong example when comparing with the existing aggs stats (they are not consumed or looked at currently). Then I wonder if what we are looking for is rather a boolean around whether a query was ever seen in a cluster. How are counts valuable if they are not comparable across different clusters? I would prefer to have no counters than counters that are hard to interpret.

> Another thing I am not sure about if we can do a deep inspection of a search request on a coordinating node to report what query types were used in it.

I wondered too. We do a rewrite on the coordinating node. Another aspect that I forgot to bring up though is that I am not sure it's a good idea to track only lucene queries after rewrite. I would think that we want to see which queries of the query DSL are used instead? 

> Alternatively, may be this type of stats should be better reside in _cluster/stats?

Good question too. If that is a better way to provide meaningful stats that need less interpretation and already aggregated, that sounds like the way to go.

There are many questions here and not many answers, let's have a high bandwidth discussion about it and try to move it forward.

Quick summary of the discussion we had: we are happy with counting at the shard level, because it gives some weight to how much data each query hits. We will look into logging the Elasticsearch query names rather than lucene queries.

> We will look into logging the Elasticsearch query names rather than lucene queries.

@javanna This turns out to be difficult to implement, as we rewrite queries so many times (on a coordinating node, in every phase of search request on shards etc). For example,  if there is a DFS phase, queries will come to shards during Query phase in already rewritten form (i.e. `ShardSearchRequest` will have `source` rewritten). I wonder if we are ok to report rewritten form, as counting queries on shards in an original form will complicate the code?

Alternatively, we can go back to an idea to count queries on a coordinating node where we have an original submitted user request (but these counts will not be per shard)?

cc @giladgal

Discussed with @giladgal, and we are ok to count rewritten queries per shard, as implemented in this PR (as it allows us to track queries that runs more frequently in practice and not queries that a user called). 
So this PR is ready for review.

cc @javanna  @jtibshirani

review_comment: Will this be false by default? Do we know what the telemetry cluster request looks like? Do they need to update their request to get the additional queries stats?

should we write a unit test for the serialization of this class. I am super nervous with these changes that we may get silly things wrong, like the version, and not realize it. Is serialization across multiple versions covered by existing tests?
should we add some basic unit test of the functionalities added to SearchExecutionContext?
I wonder why the corresponding service for aggs implements `ReportingService<AggregationInfo>`. Is a similar functionality required on the queries side of things too?
would it make sense to have a text field to execute the match query on? That way it would not get rewritten to term also.
question: what happens if we register queries from plugins providing the service? Trying to figure out if there is a way around the null invariant.

Question: is the main reason to pre-register known queries to have an immutable map and not have to deal with concurrency if we add new queries when they appear first? Or simplicity? When do we end up calling this with unknown queries? That happens with queries provided by plugins? I intuitively thought that we took care of this by not providing the service for queries registered from plugins. Do we test what happens with queries introduced by plugins?
Do we already have tests for the serialization of this class across multiple versions?

I see that existing stats are implemented as SearchOperationListener (see ShardSearchStats). Maybe these additional stats fit in that existing listener? That may also help remove the extra "SearchUsageService" dependency from SearchExecutionContext which I am not super happy with. Ideally this method returns a non-modifiable set of queries used, and the listener adds them to the usage service that's injected to it? Maybe then it makes sense to merge the existing stats holder with the additional usage service. I also noticed that we already have a CounterMetric that we may want to re-use for the counting.

I had a deeper look also at the existing search stats: they were originally made to be returned from nodes stats, then a subset of it was also exposed by cluster stats (but the search stats are not part of it). It looks like though there is existing infra to report on shard level things as part of cluster stats.

That makes me wonder: even if we collect at the shard level, does it make sense to expose these additional counters at the node level (node feature usage)? Does it add value to be able to distinguish nodes from one another? Would it make more sense to expose these aggregated through cluster stats? Would that simplify how the data is consumed,  or would that make it harder, or aggregating on the client side is easy enough? 

It would seem as moving the reporting from one API to another should not be a huge job, provided that the collection stays unchanged.
